items.title: The sum of the orders of the tame symbols over the height one primes of a two dimensional Noetherian local domain vanishes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: This is the chapter's Key Lemma for the tame symbol, stated for a two dimensional Noetherian local domain A with fraction field K and f, g in K^*: the sum of ord_{A/q}(d_{A_q}(f, g)) over the height one primes q at which f or g fails to be a unit vanishes (statement lines 18339-18367). The statement is preceded by a reference block recording that for an excellent A this is Kato's Milnor K-theory proposition, which is why the result is genuinely research-level rather than a formal manipulation. The proof first uses the additivity of the tame symbols and of the order functions to reduce to the case f = a, g = b in A (proof lines 18370-18375). Then it rewrites the sum in terms of the determinant of the two-periodic complex, using the length-determinant proposition to convert the displayed sum into the condition e_A(A/(ab), a, b) = 0 (proof lines 18376-18382), and observes that this is immediate because the complex with terms A/(ab) and the alternating maps a, b is exact (proof lines 18386-18388). The reduction to the two specialisations of f and g, and the translation of an order-theoretic sum into the vanishing of an e-invariant, are the non-formal steps, so the claim is H3.
